recorded may be the one that put the secret there. Live JPEG frames and recordings show the rendered page

items.reason: Verified against Agent, BrowserSession and Recorder; seven existing frame tests passed.
items.what: Live frame and recording secret suppression is documented as absent.
items.why: Agent._act calls withhold_frames(True) before typing secrets; _reveals updates it from observations. BrowserSession drops withheld live frames and Recorder retains its last clean frame. SECURITY.md and docs/design.md already describe this behavior.

items.what: Select options past the 240 cap are silently dropped.
items.why: A wanted option beyond the cap can never be chosen and nothing reports it.
items.reason: Remove this limit under the owner's standing rule that nothing a model, grader or trace sees is capped unless a provider documents the limit (where Jev's documented limit applies, fit to that limit by name). Done on the no-caps product branch, and the live ship check must hold or improve. Verifier: max_choice_options defaults to 240 (config.rs:115) while Jev documents 255 per Choice, and docs/jev.md line 17 itself says 'the 240 cap ... are ours'; the headroom is justified for policy choices that add escape options, but choose() adds none, so 15 offerable options are dropped for nothing. Options past the cap are dropped with no event, no escape option and no error, so a select with 300 entries can never be set to a late one and the trace does not say why. Only options above the model's real DecisionProfile limit (255, or 26 on an unknown model) are forced out by the provider, and the policy's group-then-element pattern already exists for that case.

items.what: A missing value_absent answer means the value is treated as present.
items.why: Missing answer silently becomes a decision.
items.reason: Unreachable through the client contract: every decision client (system_one.rs:116, vercel.rs:93, openai_decisions.rs:196) runs parse_answers, which errors when answer ids differ from question ids or the answer type is not noul, and the split path returns Err rather than partial answers, so evaluate() either yields Some(Answer::Noul) for 'stated' or fails. The arm is the exhaustiveness fallback the match needs. The reviewer's direction is also wrong: 0.0 would mean 'not stated', ending the field as missing, not treating the value as present.

items.what: The field writer sees a truncated history.
items.why: Same fixed-count history window applied to the LLM.
items.reason: Remove this limit under the owner's standing rule that nothing a model, grader or trace sees is capped unless a provider documents the limit (where Jev's documented limit applies, fit to that limit by name). Verifier: record() in crates/fastbrowse-agent/src/agent/helpers.rs:407 keeps only the last history_entries (6) in full plus earlier_history_entries (14) without effects, and outside that window only entries that typed or set a value; reads, clicks and navigations older than 20 steps vanish. The numbers are tuned (config.rs comments cite an eight-step form losing its first field), not documented by any provider, and here the reader is the LLM field writer, whose context is far larger. The typed-value carve-out mitigates but does not remove the window.

items.what: A failed wall quote becomes empty evidence.
items.why: The failure is swallowed.
items.reason: The fallback is deliberate and part of the function's documented contract (doc comment on `wall_quotes`: "A failed capture loses only the quote"), and it fires only on the path that is already returning `Status::Blocked` with its own error text and `WallKind::BotCheck` (driving.rs:217-231; consumed at mod.rs:503-522 as `Outcome.evidence`). Nothing downstream acts on the empty vector: no model, grader or verifier reads a Blocked result's evidence, it goes to the caller as a supplementary quote, and raising the capture error instead would replace a correct bot-check diagnosis with a browser error. The removed Python core had the same contract (`_wall_quotes` returned `()` on BrowserError). Separate from this finding: the same producer slices the quote with `WALL_QUOTE_CHARS = 600` (mod.rs:72, chunks.rs:231), a picked number, not a provider limit, that a caller agent receiving the result over MCP would see; that belongs to the arbitrary-caps lens, not to this fallback.

items.what: Jev's click is replaced by DONE once a lookup is answered.
items.why: Code overrides the model's chosen action.
items.reason: Remove or state this hidden rule to the model it overrides? Owner's direction: hidden logic that overrides a model without telling it goes. Done on the no-caps product branch with the live ship check. Verifier: Line 279 discards a click Jev chose whenever code's own `answered(plan, notes)` holds for a lookup plan (helpers.rs:157, every information requirement evidenced in notes) and forces DONE. Jev is shown `unread_requirements` (empty) and the DONE option "Every requirement is visibly satisfied" (policy.rs:62), but nothing in NEXT_ACTION_RULES tells it a click under that state is thrown away, and the step is recorded as `Decider::Llm` (code_decision, helpers.rs:756), so the trace never shows Jev's click was overridden. The damage is bounded but not free: `finish` re-judges DONE, and when the verifier refuses it calls `recover` (finishing.rs:131,273,340) or sets `open_answer_outputs` (finishing.rs:258), spending recovery budget on a decision Jev never made. No lens Do-not-flag entry (safety invariant, schema validation, stated threshold) covers it and nothing in Settled matches. The comments cite run evidence ("Select flight" click, a catalogue paged to the end, 11 of 138 0.5.7 runs), so removing or restating the rule to Jev is a design choice to evaluate, not a plain cut. Same producer as the identical override at line 261.

items.quote: decision = Decision { operation: Operation::Read, target: None, ..decision };
items.what: A pager click chosen by Jev is turned into a Read.
items.why: Code overrides the model's chosen action.
items.reason: The rule is stated to Jev: when a pager link is on the page, the read_assessment question Jev is sent says "Matching records in a paginated list are evidence ... Read those records before opening a record's detail link or leaving the list." (policy.rs:658-664), and the lens defines the defect as a rule the model is never told. The override only fires when the page is unread (`!state.read_here`), the plan still has unread information requirements, and Jev answered the read question other than Evidence (otherwise `read_before_interaction`, acting.rs:995-1033, already read and the loop continued). The substituted operation is a Read, which is non-acting, loses no information, sets `read_here` so it cannot repeat on the same page, and hands the pager decision back to Jev on the next iteration with the page's records in its notes.

items.what: The verifier's acceptance is overridden by an idle/undone rule.
items.why: Code overrides the verifier's verdict.
items.reason: The verifier is told this rule: prompts::verdict states an action requirement 'is satisfied when the steps taken show it executed on the control the task meant', and the unmet action ids reach it marked '(doubted: show it is satisfied, or name it missing)' since unmet (probability above claim_problem_above) is a subset of doubted (not below requirement_confirmed_below). The override fires only when the full history holds no executed acting step at all, the one case where the prompt's own stated condition cannot hold, so it enforces the stated rule rather than a hidden one; the lens's judgment question (would the model behave differently if told) is answered no because it was told.

items.what: A doubted lookup is accepted without the verifier.
items.why: The verifier step is skipped on a code rule justified by a run count in a comment.
items.reason: Remove or state this hidden rule to the model it overrides? Owner's direction: hidden logic that overrides a model without telling it goes. Done on the no-caps product branch with the live ship check. Verifier: check_done returns Verify when complete is below done_accept_from (or not confirmed above done_confirmed_from), a verdict from documented Jev probabilities and stated thresholds; doubt() L569-578 then silently replaces that Verify with Accept for every all-information plan with nothing unmet, no guessed address and no blocked action, so the LLM verifier never runs. The only justification is the comment 'it never did in 76 0.5.7 verifications', a sample count, not a documented limit or a prompt-stated rule, and verified() shows the skipped verifier could still have refused (complete=false naming nothing) or named ungrounded requirements. The claim check (holds) still runs, but it judges quotes against claims, not completion or page grounding, which is what the verifier was for. Fix is a design choice: record as decide, and validate removal on dev evals since it changes which runs pay for and receive a verifier verdict.

items.what: The verifier request carries a truncated visited list.

Same producer as the visited finding (ObservationLimits.history_entries + earlier_history_entries).

items.what: Requirement ids the verifier named missing are excused when the notes cite something.

Verifier: The verifier is told 'Be strict and name every requirement id that is not visibly satisfied' and doubted ids '(doubted: show it is satisfied, or name it missing)' (verification/prompts.rs, mod.rs:564), but nothing tells it that an information requirement with any notes evidence is excused unless Jev held it unmet or it was misread; verified() then accepts over its missing list. The doc comment at helpers.rs:301-306 records the flash-lite motivation, so the fix is a design choice: state the rule to the verifier or hand it the claim-check result.

Verifier: Jev reads the filtered page (driving.rs:181 passes without_failed_links into decide) and is never told the rule: NEXT_ACTION_RULES and TARGET_RULES in policy.rs say nothing about withheld links, and policy.rs:940 computes omitted_elements from the already filtered observation, so the dropped links are not even counted. const READER_TALLIES: &str = "# Tallies
For a count of records or a ranking by record count, return tally groups: each key is the label stated in its records, and each record cites its own source blocks. Choose the entity level requested by the task. When counting items inside groups, group headings and subtotals are context: cite each matching item separately. Keep other claims concise, at most 60.

items.reason: Remove or state this hidden rule to the model it overrides? Owner's direction: hidden logic that overrides a model without telling it goes. Done on the no-caps product branch with the live ship check. Verifier: Could not refute. The screenshot reaches the LLM verifier only when visual_only_state() is true (crates/fastbrowse-agent/src/agent/finishing.rs:587: `let screenshots = if visual_only_state(fresh) { self.screenshots().await? } else { Vec::new() };`); the default is to withhold it, and 40 is one of the picked numbers that opens the gate, carried over verbatim from the Python original (`len(observation.viewport_text.strip()) < 40`). No provider documents it, no config exposes it, and the verifier prompt (prompts.rs verdict(): "Decide from the set controls, page text and notes") tells the model which evidence it has but never the rule that decided it, so a page whose state sits in pixels past the heuristics (41 chars of text, no dialog, no visual control, visual_content false) is judged blind and the model cannot ask. Not covered by any Do-not-flag entry: the only legitimate withholds are in screenshots() itself (secret_on_screen, ScreenshotsUnavailable), which are a safety invariant and a host capability and stay. This is a design choice (always send the screenshot, or state the rule to the verifier), so the audit records it as decide; the producer is the visual_only_state gate at finishing.rs:587, of which the quoted 40 is one knob. Lenses arbitrary-caps and model-second

items.quote: Ok(Extraction { data: None, evidence, problem: Some(text::prefix(&error.to_string(), 500).to_string()) })
items.what: The extraction problem returned to the caller is cut to 500 characters.
items.why: Truncates the only explanation of a failed extraction with no documented reason.
items.reason: No model, grader or trace reads this value. The only consumer in the crates is crates/fastbrowse-agent/src/agent/finishing.rs:1026, `verified_ok = verified_ok && extraction.problem.is_none()`, which tests presence only; Extraction is never dumped to a trace event, the ledger or the Outcome. Under the arbitrary-caps lens's Do not flag (data no model or trace reads) the cut is not a cap on what a model sees. A separate silent-fallbacks-shaped observation, not this finding: the whole failure text is dropped, so a caller whose schema failed validation gets Status::Unverified with no reason anywhere.

items.what: The LLM verifier's output is capped at 400 tokens.
items.why: Output-token cap on the verdict; a verdict listing many missing ids is cut mid-JSON.
items.reason: Remove this limit under the owner's standing rule that nothing a model, grader or trace sees is capped unless a provider documents the limit (where Jev's documented limit applies, fit to that limit by name). Done on the no-caps product branch, and the live ship check must hold or improve. Verifier: 400 is a picked number sent as the provider output cap on every verifier call (support.rs generate -> openai_compatible.rs inserts max_tokens/max_completion_tokens when > 0; anthropic.rs likewise). A verdict listing many requirement ids plus ungrounded ids ends mid-JSON; grow_cap then spends the one retry at 4x and a second truncation is reported as LLMError::Failed, so the finish attempt fails. No provider documents 400; the repository's own TokenBudget defaults set read_output_tokens and compose_output_tokens to 0 with the comment 'fastbrowse does not cap, truncate or crop an output token', which this constant contradicts. The doc comment's justification (1166 tokens restating the answer on one live run) is a prompt problem, not a provider limit. Fix is a design choice: send 0 (no cap, the path the client already supports) and, if the restating pathology matters, say so in the verdict prompt (model-read text).

items.what: An unparseable CDP message is dropped without a log.
items.why: Its caller waits out the full deadline and the cause is invisible.
items.reason: Remove or state this hidden rule to the model it overrides? Owner's direction: hidden logic that overrides a model without telling it goes. Done on the no-caps product branch with the live ship check. Verifier: No Do-not-flag entry or Settled item covers it: nothing in the module doc or ADR 0003 documents ignoring bad frames, and the behaviour this reader claims to port (cdp-use client.py _handle_messages) does the opposite, logging an error and failing every pending future when json.loads raises. Here a text frame that is not an Incoming (non-JSON from a cloud proxy, or an id that is not a u64) is dropped on the floor while the crate's own diagnostic seam, pub(crate) warn in lib.rs (used by recording.rs and session.rs), goes unused; if the dropped frame was a reply, send waits CDP_REPLY_SECONDS, probes Browser.getVersion successfully, then reports PageUnresponsive 'the page did not answer while the browser did' and counts a deadline against the session, which misattributes the cause. The fix is one warn("a CDP message could not be parsed") call naming only the kind, never the text, since frames can carry page text or credentials.

items.what: English label list decides which links are pagers that code walks by itself.

The lens's Defect and Judgment both concern what a model, grader or trace sees, and the task's own rule says data no model, grader or trace ever reads dismisses. The TemporaryFile holding the full stderr is lost on abort, which is a human-diagnostics nicety, not an arbitrary-caps defect; the Rust core's `tail` in crates/fastbrowse-browser/src/adapters/local_chrome.rs:480 makes the same 2000-byte cut, which the harness docstring says it deliberately mirrors.

items.why: The grader (the Jev claim judge) never sees earlier posts, so a claim about a message that was sent and then followed by another post to the same path is graded on partial evidence. No Jev limit requires this. Jev allows 32k tokens of state.

Attempted refutation: today the only claim with a submitted path is contact-form, whose deterministic check (_contact, tasks.py:48-50) already requires exactly one /submit/contact post before the judge runs, and contact.html has one form, so the cap drops nothing in the current task set; that makes the impact low, not the cap justified, and the generic helper is duplicated verbatim in src/fastbrowse/evals/bench.py:154-159 (same producer, fix both). items.quote: call_seconds = sum(line.seconds or 0.0 for line in llm)
items.what: An LLM cost line with no seconds counts as 0 s in the throughput denominator, while its tokens still count.
items.why: tokens_per_second comes out inflated. That figure gates publication (publication._moves, benchmarks.regressions: 'tokens_per_second regression'), so a later build with complete timings can look like a throughput regression.
items.reason: Remove or state this hidden rule to the model it overrides? Owner's direction: hidden logic that overrides a model without telling it goes. Done on the no-caps product branch with the live ship check. Verifier: The fallback is reachable in production: a failed LLM generation records its per-attempt lines directly to the ledger (crates/fastbrowse-clients/src/openai_compatible.rs:739-742), and those lines are built by cost()/total_cost() with `seconds: None` (openai_compatible.rs:160-191) while carrying prompt and completion tokens; only a successful generation gets `seconds: Some(started.elapsed())` (line 813). CostLine's own contract says None means 'a line that is not one call, such as browser time' (src/fastbrowse/models.py:193-194), so these lines break it and _efficiency hides that: their tokens enter the numerator, zero enters the denominator, and tokens_per_second rises on exactly the runs that had a failed call. The figure feeds publication._moves via _median_metric(rows, 'tokens_per_second') (publication.py:758-770) and benchmarks.regressions (benchmarks.py:434-437), both release gates; seconds_by_call in the same model skips None lines rather than zeroing them, so the two readings of one breakdown disagree. Not refuted: no test covers _efficiency (none in tests/ mention tokens_per_second), and no Settled entry or 'Do not flag' case applies. Fix at the producer (stamp seconds on failed-attempt lines) or exclude seconds-less lines from both sums and say so in the row.

items.what: When the grader source cannot be read, the task fingerprint uses the object's name, not its code.
items.why: The fingerprint exists to force a version bump when a grader changes. On this fallback a changed grader keeps its fingerprint and version, and published rows compare across different grading rules with no warning.
items.reason: Instrumenting `inspect.getsource` while fingerprinting all 89 tasks showed the fallback never fires: `_source` is only reached for functions and classes whose `__module__` is under `fastbrowse.evals` or `parallax.browser_use`, all defined by `def`/`class` statements in files on disk. If source later became unavailable (a pyc-only install) the qualname would not equal the token hash stored in versions.json, so `mismatches()` would report every affected task as changed, which is loud, not silent; the only silent case, a dynamically created class fingerprinted without source from the start, does not exist (the one `type(...)` class, mock.py:1088, is a local never reached through a grader's globals).
